speaker: johnstewart
text: Good evening, everybody. Welcome to our City of Beaumont regular council meeting of Tuesday, February the 9th. So I'd like to call the meeting to order. Just as we get going, I'd like to acknowledge that we are pleased to be here today on the traditional territory of Treaty 6. We acknowledge all those who share a deep connection with this land. The City of Beaumont respects the histories, languages, and cultures of all of Canada's First Peoples, whether they be a First Nation, Metis, or Inuit descent, and appreciates that their presence continues to enrich Canada's vibrant communities. We are all treaty people. As we also start the meeting tonight, we do have one proclamation to read. It is Black History Month this month. So it is my pleasure to proclaim that this month, whereas the national recognition occurred on December 14th, 1995, when the House of Commons unanimously agreed to a motion presented by the Honourable John Augustine to recognize February as Black History Month. Whereas Black History Month sought to level the imbalance in historical perspective, it has become an important part of multicultural and anti-racism programs. And whereas Black History Month in Canada is essential since it educates Canadians, few Canadians know that slavery once existed in Canada or that many of the British Loyalists who came here after the American Revolution were black. And whereas Black History Month recognizes the important sacrifices and contributions of black people to the development of Canada and the world, now therefore be it resolved that I, Mayor John Stewart, do hereby proclaim February 1st to 28th, 2021 as Black History Month in the City of Beaumont, Alberta, dated this 9th day of February, 2021. So once again, thank you all for coming and for those members of the public that are watching, Councilor Monk-Hobbs-Wayne is trying to get on but is experiencing technical difficulties. So hopefully you will be joining us soon. Are there any changes to the agenda tonight, Ms. Winter?

And the recommendation administration is here with tonight is that council approve an agreement to lease lands owned by the Catholic Archdiocese of Edmonton with the terms as presented. This was something that we started to dialogue in 2020 with the local parish about the opportunity for the city to take over lease of some of their property, mainly the open grass area, otherwise known as a Debuggin Hill, as an opportunity for potential recreation programming, spontaneous use, and other cultural or city events. Those conversations continued. It went through the Rec, Culture, and Parks Advisory Committee to see if they were supportive of that. They were. And of course they had a bunch of ideas going forward as to what potentially we could do and that's on that hill on that space. I brought this topic to council or committee of the whole December 15th, 2020. And at that time it was directed to prepare a lease agreement and bring back for ratification. Since that time, administration has worked with the archdiocese and we've come up with a agreeable agreement for leasing that land for five years with an annual fee of $1. The only real caveats are from their perspective is we notify them of what our intentions are for events ahead of time. And they are hoping we do not enter in any permanent structures on the land.
